prerequisites: Knowledge and abilities in all topics of Radio-link technologies

learning_outcomes.text: Understand and analyze systems and services based on electromagnetic fields, connecting the properties and behavior of the fields to the physical structures they interact with.
Develop initial skills to design or integrate systems based on electromagnetic fields into more complex systems.
Know the properties of electromagnetic fields and the main devices that use them.
Correctly evaluate the effects of electromagnetic phenomena on the behavior of ICT (and, more generally, electronic) equipment.
Apply standard solutions to different cases and evaluate their feasibility.
Build an appropriate model of a physical situation, solve it, and interpret the mathematical solutions found.
Deal with the study, integration, and design of equipment, systems, and services that use electromagnetic fields.
Interact efficiently with designers of electromagnetic devices.

syllabus_topics: Real transmission lines and matching structures
Dielectric behavior and propagation at RF and microwaves
Theorems of reciprocity, uniqueness and equivalence
teaching_methods: Summary and testing of vector algebra and analysis, and complex number computations

assessment_methods.method: Written part (analysis and synthesis problems of small antenna arrays and radio-links)
Oral exam (discussion on one of the course topics)

assessment_rules: The final verification consists of a written part (maximum 14 points) and an oral exam (maximum 20 points). To pass the exam, a student must pass separately the written part with a minimum of 5 points and the oral part with a minimum of 12 points. The sum of the two partial marks must be at least 18. Passing requires correct knowledge, adequate ability in tool use, and minimum skills, with higher grades reflecting higher ability and skills.
